items.text: Asks how the system handles thundering herd when rate limits reset for many customers simultaneously.
Questions whether rate limit counters should be considered sensitive data requiring encryption at rest.
Raises concern about storing configuration (customer limits) separately from code, violating twelve-factor app principles.
Notes missing consideration for IPv6 transition and how rate limits apply to dual-stack clients.
Asks about rollout strategy using feature flags or canary deployments to mitigate risk.
Suggests documenting the rate limiting design decision using Architecture Decision Records format.
Questions whether rate limiting should be client-side enforceable with tokens to reduce server load.
Raises concern about geographic distribution of Redis clusters and data residency requirements for global customers.

weakAnswers: The design looks good overall, just needs some minor tweaks.
Consider adding more monitoring and alerting for better observability.
Make sure the solution is scalable for future growth.
The team should consider security implications of the rate limiting design.
Good start, but need to think about edge cases and failure scenarios.
